name: Nantucket & Martha's Vineyard
summary: Two very different islands — Nantucket's whaling-era cobblestones and the Vineyard's gingerbread cottages and clay cliffs.

lodging.name: A guesthouse in Nantucket Town / Edgartown
lodging.blurb: Both walkable harbor towns; book well ahead in season.

foodMustTry.name: Bay scallops & oysters
foodMustTry.blurb: Nantucket bay scallops are prized nationwide; slurp local oysters raw.

days.label: Day 18 — Nantucket
days.summary: The grey-shingled island 30 miles out to sea.

item.title: Nantucket Town & the Whaling Museum
item.blurb: Cobblestone streets, a candlelit whaling museum, and the sperm-whale skeleton — the wealth of the 1800s frozen in place.

item.title: Bike to 'Sconset & Brant Point
item.blurb: The rose-covered cottages of Siasconset and the little lighthouse at the harbor mouth.

days.label: Day 19 — Martha's Vineyard
days.summary: Ferry over to the larger island for cottages and cliffs.

item.title: Oak Bluffs gingerbread cottages
item.blurb: Hundreds of candy-colored Victorian 'gingerbread' cottages around the Tabernacle, plus the oldest carousel in the country.

item.title: Aquinnah Cliffs & Edgartown
item.blurb: The rainbow clay cliffs at the island's western tip, then whaling-captain mansions in Edgartown.

days.label: Day 20 — Back to the mainland, north to New Hampshire
days.summary: Ferry back, then drive north around Boston to the New Hampshire seacoast.

commute.scenicNote: A travel day: ferry to Woods Hole, then up the coast past Boston into New Hampshire.
